author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma Woodhouse was a wealthy, intelligent, and happy young woman who had lived an easy life for twenty-one years.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: She was the youngest daughter of a loving father and had been the mistress of the house since her sister married, having been raised by a kind governess after her mother died.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma and her governess, Miss Taylor, were very close friends, and Emma mostly did whatever she wanted.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma's main problems were that she had too much freedom and thought a bit too highly of herself.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma felt sad for the first time when Miss Taylor got married, and she was left alone with her sleeping father after the wedding.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Even though Emma had helped arrange the marriage to Mr. Weston, she deeply missed her friend's constant companionship.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Emma worried about being lonely because her father could not provide good conversation.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Her father was old and sickly, and though he was a nice person, he was not a stimulating companion.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: Her sister lived far away in London, so Emma knew the autumn evenings would be lonely.

author: Jane Austen
ai_plain_text: There was no one in Highbury who could replace Miss Taylor. Emma tried to be cheerful to keep her father from complaining about the marriage.
